result.rationale: The addGuests.handler.ts clearly reads booking.attendees, filters uniqueGuests against existing attendees, then performs createMany — no transaction or unique constraint shown in the diff. Two concurrent mutations can both pass the filter and insert duplicate (bookingId, email) rows. The client-side zod refine for uniqueness doesn't protect against server-side races or two different users acting concurrently. This is a verifiable race condition introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code reads booking.attendees, computes uniqueGuests based on that snapshot, then does prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}}}). There is no transaction tying the read+write together and createMany does not use skipDuplicates, so concurrent addGuests calls can both pass the pre-check and attempt to insert the same (bookingId,email). Whether this results in duplicated rows or a DB error depends on a unique constraint that is not shown in the diff, so the exact failure mode isn’t fully verifiable from the PR alone, but the race/robustness concern is real and diff-grounded.
